title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md has workflow tool blocks but lacks: Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint clause, drift detection.

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

### References
- agent-value-alignment skill: references/layer-3-runtime-prompt.md
- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)

title: Add true data-flow edges to CIR for precise composition checking
description:
The composition tracer compares caller.codomain vs callee.codomain on call edges, producing 329 noisy findings across 5 repos (all false positives). The root cause is that call edges approximate data flow, but the actual data flowing through each argument slot may differ from the containing function's return type.

This ticket tracks adding **intermediate-expression nodes** to the CIR graph — each argument expression at a call site becomes its own node with its own extracted shape. The composition analyzer then compares the argument's actual shape against the callee's expected domain slot, eliminating the dominant FP class.

Previous work (vampiro-51v) added arg_shape to edges as a mitigation, but the arg_shape is extracted from the argument expression AST, not tracked as a real CIR node. True data-flow nodes would also enable:
- Chained data-flow analysis (let x = f(); g(x))

title: Add data-flow edges and fine-grained Shape model for actionable composition checking
description:
The composition checker compares shapes on call edges (containing function vs callee), not on true data-flow edges. Even with the slot-boundary redesign and Scalar/Ref(Scalar) unification, the checker cannot produce actionable findings because:

1. No data-flow edges: each call argument creates a data-flow path from the producer expression to the callee's parameter. Currently the frontend stores arg_shape on the edge but doesn't create a separate data-flow edge or compare the actual producer's shape against the consumer's expected shape.

2. Coarse Shape model: Shape::Scalar conflates u32, f64, bool, String, (). Shape::Parameterized exists but unification rules are too strict (Vec[T] does not match [T], Vec[T] does not match String). No way to express structural compatibility for call-compatibility purposes.

Fix:
- Create data-flow edges (or annotate call edges with the producer node ID) so the analyzer compares the actual value type against what the callee expects, not the containing function's return type
- Add fine-grained scalar kinds to Shape (e.g., ScalarKind::Int, Float, Bool, Char) so u32 does not match f64
- Define Parameterized unification rules: bases that are structurally compatible (Vec / slice, String / &str via existing Ref(Scalar) rule)
- The parse_amount to apply_discount seam fixture (vampiro-yvx) must still fire with exactly 1 finding

Acceptance criteria:
- u32 does NOT unify with f64 in unify_shapes
- String parameter matches &str argument (literal "hello") and vice versa
- Vec[T] parameter matches slice[T] argument
- The parse_amount to apply_discount fixture still fires exactly 1 slot-boundary finding
- Dogfood on 6 repos shows at least one actionable composition TP (see verification commands below)
- No regressions in existing tests

Verification commands:
```
# 1. Fine-grained scalar type test
cargo test -p vampiro-seam-analysis -- unify_int_does_not_match_float

# 2. Dogfood TP check - run against wai and inspect findings
cargo run --release -- check --full --mode guidance --json --path ~/para/areas/dev/gh/charly/wai/src | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); fs=d.get('data',[]); comp=[f for f in fs if f.get('classification')=='composition-break']; print(len(comp),'composition findings'); [print(f['path'],f['line-range-start'],f['evidence']) for f in comp[:5]]"

# 3. Fixture test
cargo test -p vampiro-seam-analysis --test stress_seeded_fixtures -- fixtures_are_sound
```

See also: crates/vampiro-cir/src/shape.rs for the Shape enum, crates/vampiro-cir/src/cir.rs for CirEdge, crates/vampiro-seam-analysis/src/composition.rs for unify_shapes, crates/vampiro-rust-frontend/src/extract.rs for extract_expr_shape.

title: Add true data-flow edges to CIR graph for precise composition checking
description:

title: Julia frontend: fix find_decl_name for function definitions without type annotations
description:
The Julia frontend's find_decl_name function fails to extract function names for function definitions without type annotations. For example:

    function add(x, y)
        return x + y
    end

Produces a node named <anonymous> instead of add. The function name is inside a 'signature' child node, but find_decl_name only checks for direct 'identifier' children and 'signature'/'type_head' children via find_name_inside, which may not handle the tree-sitter-julia grammar correctly.

Impact: 
- Function call edges cannot be resolved because the callee ID (jl:...:add) doesn't match the node ID (jl:...:<anonymous>:fn_0)
- Data-flow edges (slot edges, expression nodes) are not emitted because the graph.node_by_id() check fails
- All Julia function calls produce ~100% FP composition findings

Fix: Debug the tree-sitter-julia AST structure for function definitions and update find_decl_name to correctly extract the function name from the signature child.

Verification:
    cargo test cross_language_seeded --test cross_language_seeded_fixtures -- --nocapture
    cargo test julia --test julia_integration_tests

The julia_composition_break_has_data_flow_edges test should pass after this fix, asserting >= 2 slot edges and >= 2 expression nodes for add(42, 3).

title: Clojure frontend: emit expression nodes for callees not in graph
description:
The Clojure frontend's extract_call_edges function skips ALL edge emission (including per-slot data-flow edges) when the callee is not in the graph (e.g., builtins like str, +, concat, macros like ->, go-loop). This means calls to standard library functions produce no expression nodes and no per-slot data-flow edges, even for literal arguments whose shapes can be determined statically.

Impact: Composition findings on Clojure code remain at ~100% FP because the data-flow edges are never emitted for most actual call sites.

Fix: Move the per-slot expression node emission outside the graph.node_by_id() guard. Expression nodes for arguments with known shapes should be emitted regardless of whether the callee is defined in the current file. The declaration->declaration edge (return-boundary check) should remain gated on callee existence.

Verification: cargo test cross_language_seeded --test cross_language_seeded_fixtures -- --nocapture
The clojure_composition_break_has_data_flow_edges test should pass after this fix, asserting >= 2 slot edges and >= 2 expression nodes for (add 42 3).

title: Add data-flow edges to Julia frontend (slot tracking + arg_shape + expression nodes)
description:
The Julia frontend currently emits all edges with slot=None and arg_shape=None. This means the composition analyzer falls back to the noisy return-boundary check (caller.codomain vs callee.codomain) for all Julia code, producing ~100% FPs.

## Context

The Rust frontend (vampiro-51v + vampiro-uah) is the reference pattern. It uses syn (a typed AST) for type-aware shape inference. The Julia frontend uses tree-sitter, which produces a concrete syntax tree with no type information. Shape inference is inherently limited to what the syntax tree alone can reveal.

## Work

### 1. Per-slot argument tracking
For each call expression, map each argument to its parameter position. Emit edges with slot=Some(i).

Key code: crates/vampiro-julia-frontend/src/extract.rs -- call edge creation currently sets slot=None. Change to iterate over arguments and emit one edge per argument with slot=Some(i).

### 2. Expression shape inference
Implement extract_expr_shape for Julia tree-sitter AST nodes. Tree-sitter has no type information, so inference is limited to:

- Integer literal -> Scalar(Int) -- 42
- Float literal -> Scalar(Float) -- 3.14
- String literal -> Scalar(String) -- "hello"
- Boolean literal -> Scalar(Bool) -- true
- Char literal -> Scalar(Char) -- 'x'
- Symbol reference -> if tracked via local_shapes -- x (after x = f())
- Direct function call -> callee codomain -- parse_amount(x)
- Array literal -> opaque
- Comprehension -> opaque
- Macro call -> opaque

### 3. Expression node emission
For each argument with a known shape:
1. Emit a CirNode with kind=Expression, domain=codomain=shape, effect=Plain
2. Emit an expression-to-declaration edge with slot=Some(i)
3. Keep one declaration-to-declaration edge (no slot) for the return-boundary check

Reference: crates/vampiro-rust-frontend/src/extract.rs -- emit_expression_node, visit_expr_call

### 4. Local variable tracking
Track assignment expressions to resolve variable references in subsequent arguments. The Rust frontend uses local_shapes: HashMap<String, Shape>. The Julia frontend needs an equivalent mechanism using tree-sitter cursor-based traversal.

## Verification

### Tests
Add tests to crates/vampiro-julia-frontend/tests/julia_integration_tests.rs:
- Test that multi-arg calls produce edges with slot=Some(i)
- Test that literals resolve to correct shapes
- Test that direct function call arguments resolve to callee codomain
- Test that expression nodes are created for known-shape arguments
- Test that assignment pattern resolves variable shapes

### Success criteria
- Edges from Julia code have slot=Some(i) for multi-arg calls
- At least literal, direct function call, and variable reference shapes are resolved
- Expression nodes are emitted for arguments with known shapes
- vampiro check on a Julia stress fixture produces 0 crashes and finds at least one genuine composition mismatch

The Python and Clojure frontends use ScalarKind::Unit as a fallback for all scalar types, producing 28+ composition-break findings across ecosystem dogfood (18 in python-frontend/src/extract.rs, 10 in clojure-frontend/src/law.rs and extract.rs). The evidence shows ScalarKind::Unit being compared against Option<T> and Vec<T> — the fallback prevents the composition tracer from matching real types.

Fix: add type inference for common scalar types in each frontend:
- Python: map str→ScalarKind::String, int→ScalarKind::Int, float→ScalarKind::Float, bool→ScalarKind::Bool
- Clojure: map String→ScalarKind::String, Long/Integer→ScalarKind::Int, Double→ScalarKind::Float, Boolean→ScalarKind::Bool

Success criteria: composition findings on Python/Clojure frontend files drop to 0.

title: Fix ? operator per-slot edge dedup in Rust frontend
description:
The visit_expr_try handler creates an edge with slot=None for the ? operator, but visit_expr_call creates per-slot edges (slot=0, slot=1, etc.). Since the edge ID differs (call_compose_command vs call_compose_command_slot_0), the dedup in add_edge fails — the ? operator's Unwrapped/Ordinary/Total resolution is lost, and the edge keeps Propagated (from the call visitor).

Impact: 2 swallowed-effect FPs in espectacular (runner.rs:123), plus potentially missed Unwrapped resolutions across all codebases wherever ? is used on multi-argument calls.

Fix: in visit_expr_try, when the operand is a Call or MethodCall with multiple args, emit per-slot pre-recorded edges matching what visit_expr_call will produce.

title: Refine Shape model: distinguish primitive types, strings, and containers
description:
The coarse Shape model cannot distinguish primitive types (u32 vs f64 vs String vs bool — all Scalar), cannot distinguish containers (Vec<T> vs String vs PathBuf), and conflates scalar values with references to scalars.

This causes false positives in the slot-boundary check (Vec<Scalar> vs Scalar) and prevents the return-boundary check from catching genuine type mismatches (e.g., returning u32 where f64 is expected).

Fix: add a `Str` variant for string-like types, distinguish integer vs float scalars, add a `Container { base, params }` model for Vec/Array/Slice, and allow `Container` to unify with `Scalar` when appropriate (e.g., a Vec literal used where &[T] is expected).

Acceptance criteria:
- String literal "hello" matches &str (Ref(Scalar)) AND String parameter (Scalar)
- u32 does NOT match f64
- Vec<T> does NOT match scalar (except for known conversions like Vec→&[T])
- The 9 remaining slot-boundary FPs are eliminated or confirmed genuine

title: Replace .unwrap() detection with true discard detection for swallowed-effect tracer
description:
○ vampiro-af2.2 · Replace .unwrap() detection with true discard detection for swallowed-effect tracer   [● P2 · OPEN]
Owner: charly vibes · Type: task
Created: 2026-07-29 · Updated: 2026-07-29

DESCRIPTION
The swallowed-effect tracer (REQ-9) currently fires on every .unwrap()/.expect() call, classifying them as "swallowed" effect. This produces 297 FPs across 6 repos, almost entirely in test code.

What the EARS spec actually means by "swallowed effect": discarding a Result/Option without reading it — `let _ = result_fn();` or `result_fn();` with a semicolon.

Fix: instead of flagging force-unwraps (which are panic-risks, a different concern), detect true discards by checking whether the expression's effect channel is propagated or dropped. This requires tracking whether a call's return value is used or discarded.

Acceptance criteria:

See  and  for existing discard-related test patterns.
- `let _ = result_fn();` produces a swallowed-effect finding
- `result_fn().unwrap()` does NOT produce a swallowed-effect finding (it's a panic risk, handled elsewhere)
- Test code `.unwrap()` statements produce 0 findings

title: Refine Shape model: string literals should match &str parameters (slot-boundary FP)
description:
The coarse Shape model maps all string types (String literals, &str, String, etc.) to a mix of `Shape::Scalar` and `Shape::Ref(Box::new(Shape::Scalar))`. The slot-boundary check fires false positives when a string literal (mapped to `Shape::Scalar`) is passed to a function expecting `&str` (mapped to `Shape::Ref(Scalar)`).

Dogfood-8 shows 1323 remaining slot-boundary findings, all with this `produced=Scalar vs expected=Ref(Scalar)` pattern.

Options:
1. Add `Shape::Str` variant — distinct from Scalar, unified with Ref(Scalar) in unify_shapes
2. Add `Shape::Literal` classification — more general, covers string literals, char literals
3. Make unify_shapes treat Scalar as matching Ref(Scalar) — simplest but may over-generalize

Acceptance criteria:
- Slot-boundary findings at or below return-boundary count (currently 338)
- parse_amount→apply_discount fixture still fires exactly 1 finding
- String literal arguments to &str parameters produce no findings

title: Redesign slot-boundary checker: compare intermediate expression type, not containing function's return type
description:
The slot-boundary check (vampiro-51v) compares `caller.codomain` (the containing function's return type) against `callee.domain[slot]` (what the callee expects at that parameter position). This is structurally wrong: the value flowing through the slot is an intermediate expression, not the outer function's return type.

Consequence: dogfood-4 shows the check produces 3906 false positives across the ecosystem (21x increase vs dogfood-2), all of the form "function returning () called a function expecting &str/f64/etc. at some parameter."

Design options:
1. Add intermediate-expression CIR nodes - the frontend creates a node for each call argument expression, and edges from that node carry the expression's actual type. Cost: high (schema change, frontend rework).
2. Frontend-side slot annotation - the frontend computes the type of each argument and stores it on the edge (CirEdge.arg_shape: Option<Shape>). The analyzer compares arg_shape against domain_slot. Cost: medium.
3. Bounding the slot check - only fire when the slot edge's source node has the same codomain as what is expected at the slot (i.e., the function returns the value it passes). Cost: low but may miss genuine seams.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dogfood results show <80% FP rate for composition-break findings after the fix
- The parse_amount→apply_discount seam fixture (vampiro-yvx) still fires exactly 1 slot-boundary finding
- Existing return-boundary behavior is preserved

title: Composition analyzer: add slot-boundary check (callee domain[slot] vs caller codomain)
description:

## Scope

1. In `crates/vampiro-seam-analysis/src/composition.rs`, after the existing return-boundary check (codomain vs codomain), add a slot-boundary check:

   - Compare the caller's codomain against `callee.domain[n]` using `unify_shapes`
   - On mismatch, emit a new `composition-break` finding with evidence showing the slot, the expected domain shape, and the produced shape
2. Add a finding variant or reuse `CompositionMismatch` with the slot information in evidence

title: Approve data-flow edge representation (slot on CirEdge vs separate edge type)
description:
Resolve how per-slot argument binding is represented in CIR.

## Options

### Option A: Optional slot field on CirEdge
Add `slot: Option<u32>` to `CirEdge`. Existing edges get `None` (backward-compatible). The composition analyzer checks slot-bearing edges by comparing `caller.codomain` against `callee.domain[slot]`.

- Pro: minimal schema change, no new types
- Con: mixes call-flow semantics with data-flow semantics on one edge type
- Con: a call site passing multiple arguments needs multiple edges (one per slot)

### Option B: Separate DataFlowEdge type
Add a new `DataFlowEdge` struct with `source_value: StableId` (which node produces the flowing value), `target: StableId` (which node consumes it), `slot: u32`. The composition analyzer iterates data-flow edges instead of call edges for slot-boundary checks.

- Pro: clean separation of call-graph vs data-flow concerns
- Pro: naturally handles multi-argument calls (multiple DataFlowEdges per call site)
- Con: larger schema change, frontends need to emit two edge types

## Decision criteria
- Backward compatibility with existing CIR graphs
- Frontend implementation cost (especially Python/Clojure/Julia)
- Analyzer implementation complexity
- Clarity for downstream consumers

Record decision in `docs/decisions/data-flow-edges.md`.,
notes: Decision recorded in docs/decisions/data-flow-edges.md. Selected Option A: slot: Option<u32> on CirEdge. Bumped CIR schema to 0.2.0.

title: Carry per-slot argument binding on CIR edges for composition analysis
description: The composition tracer (0vb.4.2) operates over frontend call edges (source=caller, target=callee), which approximate the EARS data-flow edge. Without per-slot argument-to-parameter binding on CirEdge, the coarse check compares callee.codomain against caller.domain (whole parameter list). unify_shapes is correct; the wiring is the approximation. Add an optional argument-slot field to CirEdge (or a companion data-flow edge type) so the composition tracer compares the callee's codomain against the specific caller parameter slot that consumes it. Removes spurious findings on multi-param callers and enables precise parse_amount→apply_discount seam detection.
acceptance_criteria: CIR edges carry the consuming parameter slot (or a data-flow edge variant exists); CompositionAnalyzer compares callee.codomain against that slot only; E2E fixture produces exactly one finding on the parse_amount→apply_discount seam with no spurious findings on the caller's own-parameter edges; workspace tests, fmt, clippy clean.

Bump to the latest action major versions that target Node 24. Verify workflow syntax after bumping.

title: Doctor config test uses wrong config format
description:
**File:** `crates/vampiro-cli/src/doctor.rs:244–249`

Test writes `[scan]\nthreads = 4\n` which would be rejected by `Config`'s
`deny_unknown_fields` + kebab-case parser. Test passes only because
`ConfigCheck` doesn't actually parse with `Config`.

**Fix after the doctor config-check issue:** Once `ConfigCheck` uses
`Config::read()`, update test to write `scan-threads = 4`.

title: `vampiro-law` and `vampiro-lifecycle-analysis` are orphaned workspace members
description:
**File:** `Cargo.toml` workspace

Both crates exist in the workspace and are tested but are dependencies of no
other crate. Features they implement (law verification, lifecycle analysis) are
advertised in README/EARS spec but not accessible via the CLI.

**Fix (documentation):** Add a "Not yet integrated" note to README.
**Fix (code):** Wire them into `vampiro-cli` when ready.

title: Adopt genesis modules (doctor, feedback, cli, status, scaffold, guide, discovery)
description:
## Context

genesis-vibes provides shared CLI infrastructure across the charly-vibes tool suite. v0.4.0 adds the full set of modules.

## Modules to adopt

### Existing (from earlier versions)
- **genesis::doctor**: Diagnostic framework with auto-fix support
- **genesis::feedback**: Agent issue reporting
- **genesis::cli**: Completions generation, version-json pre-parse
- **genesis::status**: Cross-tool status dashboard (StatusContributor trait)
- **genesis::scaffold**: Init scaffolding builder

### New in v0.4.0
- **guide::CliVerbosity**: Standard `-v`/`-vv`/`-vvv` + `-q`/`--quiet` flags
- **guide::CliFormat**: `--json`/`--human` with TTY auto-detect (JSON for agents/pipes)
- **guide::OutputFormat / Output::emit() / Guide::run_formatted()**: Unified format dispatch
- **discovery module**: Register vampiro in `.genesis/tools.toml` for cross-tool discovery

## Tasks

- [ ] Bump genesis-vibes dependency to '0.4'
- [ ] Adopt genesis::doctor for health checks
- [ ] Adopt genesis::feedback for agent issue reporting
- [ ] Adopt genesis::cli for completions and version-json
- [ ] Implement StatusContributor for cross-tool status
- [ ] Adopt genesis::scaffold for init command
- [ ] Adopt guide::CliVerbosity and guide::CliFormat
- [ ] Use Guide::run_formatted() for format-dispatching commands
- [ ] Register vampiro in .genesis/tools.toml

title: Upgrade genesis adoption: doctor, status, scaffold, aix
description:
## Context

vampiro already uses genesis for envelope, config, guide, managed_block,
and aix. New modules are available to add diagnostic and scaffolding tools.

## Adoption Items

### 1. Doctor framework (genesis::doctor)
vampiro doesn't have a `doctor` subcommand yet, but could benefit from one.
- Add a `doctor` subcommand using `DoctorCheck` for config validation,
  CI workflow presence, project state
- Use `DoctorRunner` to orchestrate

### 2. Status contributor (genesis::status)
vampiro doesn't have a status command.
- Implement `StatusContributor` for vampiro
- Surface config state, scan history
- Use `DoctorStatusBridge` to surface doctor health

### 3. Init scaffolding (genesis::scaffold)
vampiro has no `init` command currently.
- If adding init, use `Scaffold` builder for directory + config creation

## Note

vampiro is the most minimal genesis adopter. Focus should be on:
1. Adding a doctor subcommand (new capability)
2. Implementing StatusContributor for cross-tool integration

## Priority

P3 — new capability rather than replacement, lower urgency

title: Julia frontend: duplicate node IDs for anonymous functions
description:
When multiple anonymous functions exist in the same file, the Julia frontend generates node IDs like 'jl:.../file.jl:<anonymous>' without disambiguation, causing duplicate node IDs.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests:
  - cross_language_julia_web_server: multiple '<anonymous>' collisions
  - cross_language_julia_data_analysis: same issue

Fix: include the line number or a counter in the stable ID for anonymous functions.
close_reason: Added node counter to stable ID for anonymous functions in extract.rs

title: Python frontend: edges reference non-existent nodes for builtins like getattr
description:
The Python frontend creates edges to builtin functions (e.g. getattr) that are not extracted as graph nodes. This produces invalid edges whose targets don't exist.

Fix: filter out edges to builtin/non-extractable symbols, or extract them as graph nodes with a 'builtin' flag.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests (data_pipeline.py: getattr).
close_reason: Added graph.node_by_id check before adding call edges in process_call_expression; builtins without graph nodes are now filtered out

title: Clojure frontend: edges reference non-existent nodes for macros and constructors
description:
The Clojure frontend creates edges to nodes that were not extracted (macro calls, constructor calls). The following symbols appear as edge targets but have no corresponding node:
  - 'when-not' (macro, in data_processing.clj)
  - 'go-loop' (macro, in async_example.clj)
  - '->Response' (record constructor, in http_server.clj)

Fix: either extract these as graph nodes, or suppress edges to non-extractable symbols.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests.
close_reason: Added graph.node_by_id check before adding call edges in extract_call_edges; macros and constructors without graph nodes are now filtered out

title: Python frontend: duplicate node IDs for __init__ across classes
description:
When multiple classes in the same file define __init__, the Python frontend generates node IDs like 'py:.../cli.py:__init__' without class disambiguation, causing duplicate node IDs.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests:
  - cross_language_python_cli: Command.__init__ and Group.__init__ collide
  - cross_language_python_http_lib: Session.__init__ and HTTPErrorV.__init__ collide

Fix: include class name in the node stable ID, e.g. 'py:.../cli.py:Command.__init__' vs 'py:.../cli.py:Group.__init__'.
close_reason: Added class_name parameter to process_function_definition; method node IDs now include class prefix to avoid collisions
